resources.string: Why nearby device permission is needed

Scanning discovers nearby devices through their Bluetooth broadcasts. After connecting, the app reads heart rate, battery, temperature and other readings. On Android 12 and above only Nearby devices is requested; scan results are not used for location.

Sends local alerts when a rule triggers (signal below threshold, device disconnected, bond lost). A persistent notification is also shown during background collection. If denied, rules are still recorded but no reminder is sent.

On Android 11 and below, the system requires location permission to scan for BLE devices. This app does not use or collect location data, and location never leaves the device. This system is Android 12 or above, so scanning does not depend on location and this step will not request it.

On Android 11 and below, the system requires location permission to scan for BLE devices (a system restriction). This app uses it only to scan for devices; it does not use or collect location data, and location never leaves the device.

What if the Transfer Code is rejected?

A Transfer Code is 8 uppercase letters and digits; the input is converted to uppercase automatically. Check for extra spaces and make sure the code has not expired. Generating a new code invalidates the old one immediately. Too many attempts trigger rate limiting, and the screen shows the remaining wait time.
The device is found but connection fails. What should I do?

Make sure Bluetooth is on, and confirm scan and connect permissions under Profile → Permission check. Android 11 and below also need location permission; connection fails if any permission is missing. If it still fails, unpair the device in system Bluetooth settings and scan again from Home.
Readings stop refreshing or the chart has no new data?

Readings are written only while the device is connected, through its notify characteristics. The chart shows local stored records: synced data is kept for 7 days, while unsynced records are retained. Reconnect from the device detail screen and watch for new readings.
The server version wins, and the local pending change is replaced; Profile → Sync status shows the latest conflict count. If you need to keep local edits, continue editing after the sync completes.
How do I leave a household?

A regular member can leave directly from Profile → Household; shared devices of that household are then removed from this device. An owner with other members cannot leave directly (the server returns 409). Transfer ownership to another member, or remove the other members first, then leave.
